chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-bukhtaj, so he said: 'If it is sweet and dyes the vessel, and its owner said: Two-thirds have gone and one-third remains, then drink it.'

key_terms.الْبُخْتِجِ: Vinegar or sour wine, a common fermented drink

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for drinking vinegar that has been stored in a vessel and partially consumed?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding *al-bukhtaj* (a type of vinegar or fermented drink), establishing its permissibility when specific physical and quantitative conditions are met. The criteria—sweetness, dyeing the vessel, and the owner's claim that two-thirds have been consumed or evaporated leaving one-third—serve as indicators of purity and sufficient transformation, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on empirical signs (*al-alamat*) in determining the status of liquids.
